title: ask-sculpting-quarterly-prep-noelle-tran
content:
Context:
- Purpose: sculpt a concise, evidence-backed ask for my Q1 manager sync + calibration prep. Want pragmatic asks (headcount + manager training + small lift to measure impact) rather than open-ended wishes.
- Background: joined people-ops in late 2023, led onboarding refresh (beta launched Q2 2024), ran pilot mentorship cohort (10 mentors/18 mentees) in 2025.

Topline ask (two-sentence summary):
- Request 1 (primary): +0.8 FTE contractor (6–9 month) focused on program ops for mentorship/onboarding improvements (cohort admin, async curriculum, metrics automation).
- Request 2 (secondary, conditional): $35k pilot budget for manager training + external facilitator (2 workshops + on-demand content) to improve new-manager ramp and 1:1 quality.

Why this matters (short bullets I can speak to):
- Scalability pain: mentorship admin is currently ~6 hrs/wk taken from my time and volunteers (evidence: calendar capture shows 24 admin hours/month).
- Signal of impact: mentee survey Net Promoter-like score improved from 24 -> 42 in pilot; 70% reported at least one behavior change at 8 weeks.
- Recruitment/leverage: improved onboarding correlates with decreasing time-to-productivity (internal measure) — our cohort 1 new hire ramp median 7.2 weeks vs org median 9.4 (small n yet but positive).

Evidence (concise bullets with numbers I will cite):
- Mentor/mentee participation: 18 mentees, 10 mentors, 85% completion of core curriculum (n=18).
- Survey outcomes: mentee satisfaction 4.1/5, mentor satisfaction 4.0/5; reported behavior change 70% (post-program).
- Calendar / cost estimate: current admin load ~24 hrs/month = ~0.6 FTE of volunteer time; contractor at $75/hr x 20 hrs/week = ~$31k for 6 months (rounded).
- Manager signal: 12 managers indicated interest in structured 1:1 coaching; 4 volunteered to host case clinics.

Narrative scripts (two quick versions for manager):
- 15s version: "I want a short-term ops hire and a small training budget to convert the pilot mentorship and onboarding wins into repeatable, measurable programs. With a contractor and a $35k pilot we can automate metrics, free volunteer time, and run manager training that should move new-hire ramp and manager 1:1 quality in Q2."
- 60s version (if asked for details): "The pilot showed strong engagement and early signals on ramp time and behavior change, but it's fragile: admin is eating up volunteer hours and my cycles. Hiring a contractor for 6–9 months (program ops + metrics) plus a $35k facilitator budget lets us (1) scale to run 3 cohorts in the next 12 months, (2) automate program metrics so we can show impact to recruiting and finance, and (3) run two manager workshops to standardize onboarding handoffs. I estimate payback in reduced time-to-productivity and improved retention in 6–12 months if we measure cohort-by-cohort."

Career context (why this ask is aligned to my growth):
- This ask shows productization and owner-ship at the org level: program design -> measurable outcomes -> stakeholder alignment (recruiting, eng managers).
- Win helps demonstrate leadership scope outside execution — useful signal for next calibration.

Potential objections I expect and responses:
- Objection: "Can we deprioritize until headcount cycles?" -> Response: "This is a 6–9 month contractor ask with minimal burn that buys metrics automation; it's reversible and reduces volunteer hours now."
- Objection: "Budget is tight." -> Response: "Pilot budget is $35k with clear success criteria (ramp delta, net promoter, manager adoption) — we sunset if no signal after first 2 cohorts."

Success metrics (what I will report back in 6 months):
- Onboarding completion rate for core curriculum (target 90% completion).
- Median time-to-productivity delta vs baseline (target reduce by 1–2 weeks).
- Manager 1:1 quality: % of managers adopting structured agenda (target 40% adoption among managers who take training).
- Volunteer time freed (hrs/month) tracked via calendar capture (target reduce volunteer admin by 60%).

Action plan + timeline (what I will do if approved):
- Week 1: finalize contractor JD + scope, share with recruiting; finalize workshop SOW with facilitator options.
- Weeks 2–4: hire contractor / onboard; collector automation scope doc (metrics, data owners).
- Month 2: run first manager workshop; run cohort scheduling for mentorship.
- Month 3–6: iterate cohorts, instrument metrics, consolidate monthly brief for stakeholders (recruiting, finance).

Open questions / decisions I need from manager today:
- Prioritization: greenlight contractor search now vs push to next hiring window?
- Budget approval guardrails: do I need explicit PO for $35k or can I run pilot within existing L&D pool?
- Stakeholder ask: can recruiting commit 2 hrs/month of data/time to help feed metrics?

Quick lines to put in the sync notes (copy/paste):
- "Ask: 0.8 FTE contractor (6–9 months) + $35k pilot for manager training to scale mentorship/onboarding. Goal: measurable ramp improvement and reduce volunteer admin."
- "Success criteria: onboarding completion, ramp delta, manager adoption, volunteer time freed; will report monthly and recommend next step after 2 cohorts."

Draft follow-up email subject/body (short):
- Subject: "Follow-up: mentorship + onboarding pilot ask (+ contractor + pilot budget)"
- Body: "Thanks for the sync — per discussion, I'm drafting scope for a 6–9 month contractor to run mentorship & onboarding ops and a $35k pilot for manager training. I will circulate the JD and a short success-criteria doc by EOD Thursday for quick review."

Quick evidence appendix (placeholders I will paste into Confluence):
- pilot-survey-aggregate.csv (satisfaction + behavior change)
- calendar-admin-time-export.csv (Nov 2025–Jan 2026)
- cohort-ramp-vs-baseline.xlsx

Notes-to-self (loose / small TODOs):
- Pull calendar admin export and compute volunteer hours this week.
- Draft contractor JD with clear deliverables (metrics dashboard, cohort ops, curriculum maintenance).
- Confirm facilitator shortlist with Asha by Wed.
- Prepare a 1-slide visual: current friction -> intervention -> expected signal (for manager deck).

Emotion / framing cues (reminders to use in sync):
- Be concise; lead with the ask and the quick ROI.
- Be explicit about reversibility — pilot framed as low-risk.
- Use concrete numbers (hours saved, ramp weeks) — managers respond to measurable bets.

End of scratchpad.
